principles: Fail closed before worktree creation for missing or failed user-confirmed scope boundaries.
Keep semantic anti-expansion separate from later diff/file scope enforcement.
Reviewer influence must be auditable proposal evidence, not direct scope mutation.
Gate-consumed facts require typed registry and contract verification.
drivers: Prevent multi-agent loops from amplifying a wrong story boundary.
Minimize token waste by stopping in INIT before worktree/development.
Preserve compatibility with existing init-check and scope-contract flows.
Keep implementation narrow enough to land safely despite touching lifecycle gates.

options.name: A: Add dedicated INIT scope-boundary and freeze-check gate
pros: Blocks semantic scope creep before worktree creation
Keeps reviewer expansion explicit through proposals
cons: Adds new artifacts and CLI commands
Requires focused smoke and contract tests

options.name: B: Reuse existing scope_contract and guard_session only
cons: Does not capture original user-confirmed semantic boundary
Cannot stop token-heavy work before INIT_CHECK

options.name: C: Prompt-only reviewer discipline
cons: Fails when agents forget or misapply prompt guidance

chosen: A: Add dedicated INIT scope-boundary and freeze-check gate
rationale: Option A is the only design that mechanically freezes the user-confirmed semantic boundary before INIT_CHECK while preserving existing later file-scope gates. It costs more schema/test work, but it directly addresses the incident and Lattice core value of bounded closure.

preMortem.scenario: Missing boundary is treated as allow-all scope.
preMortem.trigger: story_create omits scopeBoundary or an older story lacks the new artifact.
preMortem.consequence: INIT_CHECK proceeds and the gate gives a false sense of safety.
preMortem.mitigation: canEnterInitCheck and getGuardFailureReason fail closed on missing scope-boundary/execution-boundary except explicit legacy compatibility paths documented as non-enforcing.

preMortem.scenario: Excluded keyword matcher blocks legitimate stories.
preMortem.trigger: Authority or Layer4 appears in a feature story that is actually about that domain.
preMortem.consequence: False positives make Lattice feel arbitrary and operators bypass the gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Default future denylist applies only to correctness_fix mode; other modes use user-confirmed excludedScope/excludedKeywords, and explicit proposal/decision can accept scope changes.

preMortem.scenario: Reviewer proposal path becomes a hidden checklist mutation channel.
preMortem.trigger: scope_extension_proposal writes accepted state or checklist changes directly.
preMortem.consequence: INIT reviewer expands scope despite the new gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Separate proposal from decision; only scope_extension_decide can accept/reject, acceptance invalidates freeze-check and requires rerun.

preMortem.scenario: Process-fact registry drifts from command behavior.
preMortem.trigger: New commands write gate evidence but registry/contract verifier is not updated.
preMortem.consequence: The gate becomes prompt-only or invisible to process audits.
preMortem.mitigation: Add L4 entries, artifact refs, required semantics, and update verify-process-fact-contract as part of CHK-005.
